nh_wm_kancamagus_eastern.blurb: These cliffs lie scattered through the forest along the eastern end of the Kancamagus Highway in New Hampshire's White Mountains. Bouldering makes up about half of the climbing here, trad most of the rest, with a smaller batch of sport routes. Boulder problems run from V0 up to V10, and roped climbs range from easy up into the 5.12s and 5.13s, with most sitting between 5.7 and 5.12. Sundown Ledge is the hub, with a big boulder collection and a steep main wall of sport lines. Woodchuck Ledge adds trad on its Diamond and Zonkers walls, and Rainbow Slabs offers gentle, thinly protected slab climbing. Many smaller cliffs see few visitors, so quiet days are easy to find.

az_6_mid_mountain.blurb: Mid-Mountain sits partway up Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains above Tucson, at about 7,000 feet, where ponderosa pine forest gives relief from the desert below. Sport routes make up roughly two thirds of the climbing, with a solid helping of trad and a modest number of boulder problems. Sport lines cluster around 5.9 to 5.11, with plenty of easier and harder options at either end. Munchkinland is the busiest sport zone, with walls facing different ways so you can chase sun or shade, and it climbs best from about April to October. Boneyard, Palisade Park and Barnum Rock add more variety across a spread-out collection of crags.

co_rifle_mountain_park.blurb: Rifle Mountain Park is a narrow, steep-walled canyon at roughly 7,000 feet, cut by East Rifle Creek into dolomitic limestone. Nearly everything here is single-pitch sport climbing on overhanging walls and in caves, with pockets, edges and pinches and a lot of technical, sustained movement. The grade range runs from the high 5.7s to 5.14, but the bulk of the routes fall between 5.12 and 5.13, with a decent set of 5.10s and 5.11s for climbers building up. The canyon runs north to south, so you can shift between sun and shade through the day. The main season stretches from mid-April to mid-November, though spring seepage can leave some lines wet, and cooler days suit the hardest routes. Ruckman Cave, Anti-Phil Wall and Project Wall are among the largest walls.

wa_southeast_cascades_yakima.blurb: This region gathers the climbing east of the Cascade crest around Yakima, and the Tieton River holds most of it. Those crags are strung along about twenty miles of the drainage on the range's east slope, on andesite from an ancient lava flow. Trad and sport are split almost evenly, with a smaller set of boulder problems, and most routes fall between 5.9 and 5.11. The lower canyon is dry country of sagebrush and oak with more crack climbing, while the higher crags stand in pine and fir forest and lean toward sport. Most walls pick up some shade, which helps in summer. Horsethief Butte, on basalt columns in the Columbia Gorge, adds top-rope laps, easy boulders and a few trad cracks.

ca_barstow_area.blurb: Climbing near Barstow means the high desert, and almost all of it is one big sport area in the hills south of town, at about 3,700 feet. Sport routes account for the great majority, with a thin scattering of trad, top-rope and boulder problems, plus a few climbs at Fort Irwin and in the Calico Mountains. The rock is volcanic in origin and full of holds: huecos, pockets, edges, jugs and crimps. Routes tend to be steep and varied, calling for both strength and careful sequences. Grades start easy and top out above 5.13, but the heart of the area is 5.10 and 5.11, with a healthy number of 5.7 to 5.9 routes too. Walls face every direction, and the season runs from October through May.

ar_sam_s_throne_surroundings.blurb: Tucked into the Boston Mountains of north-central Arkansas, near Jasper, this cluster of crags sits within the Ozark-St. Francis National Forest. The rock is hard sandstone, and sport and trad are almost evenly matched, with a smaller set of boulder problems. Most roped routes fall between 5.9 and 5.12. Sam's Throne itself is where Ozark climbing began, an exposed ridge with pines below and clean faces above, and it keeps a traditional feel with only a few sport lines. Cave Creek, across from it, is a cliff band with many fine routes of both kinds. Candy Mountain is known for tall, harder sport lines, and Valley of the Blind has some of the best bolted climbing in the state.
